body:
## Pull request overview

This PR completes multiple ROADMAP items (P2.3–P4.3) by adding accessibility attributes to key views, expanding robustness/performance/test coverage across plugins, and introducing documentation infrastructure via TypeDoc and Storybook deployment.

**Changes:**
- Add ARIA roles/labels to Kanban + Calendar views and introduce WCAG contrast verification tests.
- Add new benchmark/view-state/integration/snapshot tests across plugins and components, plus new Storybook “edge case” stories.
- Add TypeDoc configuration + `docs:api` script and a GitHub Pages Storybook deploy workflow.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 23 out of 24 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

This `aria-label` uses `toLocaleDateString("default", ...)` instead of the `locale` prop (which defaults to "default"). Use the `locale` variable here so assistive text matches the selected locale.

`h3` is given an `id` (`kanban-col-*`) but the column container uses `aria-label` rather than referencing that heading, so the `id` is currently unused. Consider switching the column container to `aria-labelledby` pointing at the heading (or remove the `id`) to avoid dead attributes and keep labeling consistent.

`ObjectRenderer` does not appear to be exported by `@object-ui/react` (the package exports `SchemaRenderer`). This Getting Started example will fail to compile; update the import/usage to the supported renderer component, and align the example schema `type` strings with the lowercase identifiers used across the repo (e.g. `type: 'card'`, `type: 'text'`).

This story introduces non-English (Arabic) user-facing strings, but the repo policy requires English-only text in docs/stories/UI labels. Keep `dir="rtl"` for layout testing, but replace the literal Arabic titles/descriptions/buttons with English placeholders so the codebase remains English-only.

This story introduces non-English (Arabic) user-facing strings, but the repo policy requires English-only text in docs/stories/UI labels. Keep `dir="rtl"` to test RTL layout, but use English placeholder content for `title`/`description`.

`role="row"`/`role="columnheader"` are being applied outside of the element with `role="grid"`. In ARIA, `row`/`columnheader` need to be contained within a `grid`/`table` (typically via a `rowgroup`). Either move the weekday header markup inside the grid structure or remove these roles to avoid invalid ARIA.
```suggestion
      <div className="grid grid-cols-7 border-b">
        {weekDays.map((day) => (
          <div
            key={day}
```

This `aria-label` uses `toLocaleDateString("default", ...)`, ignoring the `locale` prop that the component supports. This makes screen-reader labels inconsistent with the visible, locale-aware header; pass `locale` into `MonthView` and use it for label formatting.
```suggestion
              aria-label={`${day.toLocaleDateString(locale ?? undefined, { weekday: "long", month: "long", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" })}${dayEvents.length > 0 ? `, ${dayEvents.length} event${dayEvents.length > 1 ? "s" : ""}` : ""}`}
```
